card_title: Nobody Else's Faith Can Save You
description: Even Noah, Daniel, and Job couldn't save anyone but themselves. Every person has to deal with God for themselves.
excerpt: Being from a Christian family doesn't cover you. Being a good person doesn't cover you. The gap between knowing about God and knowing Him is bigger than we like to admit.
verse: "Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were there, their righteousness would save no one but themselves, says the Sovereign Lord."
body_html:
Ezekiel is being told something sobering. Even if the three most righteous men in the Old Testament, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were standing in the middle of a sinful nation, their righteousness wouldn't save anybody but themselves. In a later verse God says even their own sons and daughters wouldn't be covered.

Every person has to deal with God for themselves.

That's hard for most of us. We like the idea that growing up in a godly home means we're covered, that marrying a strong Christian pulls us in with them, that showing up at church makes us one of God's own. None of that saves anyone.

The Bible actually says many will stand before God calling Him Lord, and He'll reply that He never knew them. That's one of the scariest verses in Scripture. It isn't there to make us live in fear. It's there to draw us toward a real relationship with a God who wants to actually know us, not just know of us.

Being from a Christian family doesn't cover you. Being a good person doesn't cover you. Your parents' faith, your spouse's faith, your pastor's faith, none of it transfers. The gap between knowing about God and knowing Him is bigger than we like to admit.

Social media makes that gap even easier to hide. There are more people than ever posting Bible verses, quoting sermons, sharing worship songs, and showing up with the right language. Some of them are walking with God. Some of them aren't. There's no way to tell from the outside. The gauge of someone's faith has never been their posts or their platform. It's their actual relationship with the Lord.

That includes me. That includes you.

It's easier now than it's ever been to look like a Christian without actually being in a real relationship with Jesus. That's why Ezekiel 14 matters even more today. At the end of your life, your highlight reel isn't going to save you. Noah's righteousness wasn't enough to carry anyone else. Neither was Daniel's. Neither was Job's. And nobody else's can carry you either.

You have to know Him for yourself.

Do you know God, or do you just know a lot about Him?
question: Do you know God, or do you just know a lot about Him?
